transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Liam (CSM), Dr. Maya Ruiz (Summit), Ethan Park, Priya Menon

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me I have Samira our solutions engineer and Liam who helps with onboarding. How are you all?
[00:08] Maya: Hi, afternoon. Good, thanks. We've got Ethan and Priya here as well. We're hoping to get clarity on a few security points before we move into procurement.
[00:15] Jordan: Totally. The agenda we sent over — quick posture overview, dive into KMS and private deployment options, and then address prompt retention and the training question directly. Anything to add?
[00:23] Ethan: That covers it. Also timeline: procurement wants to know whether SOC 2 Type II and ISO artifacts are available for review and whether we can get a DPA.
[00:29] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll go through each.

Summary / key asks (auto notes):
- Confirm Redwood’s SOC 2 / ISO status and provide reports (customer to review)
- Explain RBAC/SSO integration and audit log retention windows
- Detail KMS options for key ownership and BYOK (bring-your-own-key) support
- Confirm explicit "no training" commitment and data retention for prompts/attachments
- Discuss private deployment (VPC / on-prem) timelines and feasibility

[02:05] Samira (Redwood SE): Quick intro from me — technical lead on private deployments. For context, Redwood offers hosted, dedicated, and private options. For regulated workloads we generally recommend Private (VPC) or Dedicated with customer-managed keys depending on the data residency and control needs.
[02:22] Priya: On that, a clarification: when you say private, do you mean the control plane still touches metadata, or is everything customer-customer in the VPC?
[02:31] Samira: Great question. For our Private offering the control plane is customer-managed in the VPC — the customer has network-level control and can optionally run the inference runtime entirely in their subnet. We can also offer an air-gapped on-prem package for highly regulated environments. There are tradeoffs in maintenance and patching cadence there.
[02:50] Maya: And for SOC 2 and ISO — what certification levels do you have and are those documents shareable under an NDA?
[02:58] Jordan: We have SOC 2 Type II, and an ISO 27001 alignment summary. We can share the SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO package under our standard NDA or a mutual NDA; we'll attach the SOC 2 attestation and the ISO scope document.
[03:12] Ethan: Good. Also, audit logs — retention and what’s included: Are request/response payloads stored in logs or just headers/metadata? Our legal team is sensitive about PHI being present in logs.
[03:22] Samira: Default logs capture request IDs, latency, model used, token counts, and high-level route metadata. By default we do not persist full request/response payloads in operational logs — those are stored only if customers opt into extended retention for debugging or benchmarking. For Private deployments you can disable payload ingestion entirely.
[03:42] Maya: When you say "stored only if customers opt in" — is that a console toggle or does it require a contract addendum?
[03:48] Samira: It’s a config toggle for hosted/dedicated customers with the right entitlements. For enterprise contracts we'll include explicit settings in the DPA so it's contractually restricted.

[04:20] Jordan: Let's address the big one — training on customer data. Straight answer: Redwood does not use customer prompt/response data to train or fine-tune our base models. We can provide a legal commitment in the DPA and a technical description of isolation.
[04:34] Ethan: Do you redact or otherwise process PII before any telemetry is captured? For example, if someone sends a patient record in a prompt, is that material ever used?
[04:43] Samira: We have a two-tier approach. Short-term telemetry for debugging is ephemeral and under strict access controls, and for hosted setups it's kept for X days (we'll provide exact retention numbers) — but it is not used for training. For Private/VPC we support no-telemetry modes where nothing is exfiltrated from the VPC; in Dedicated you can enable customer-managed KMS and opt out of telemetry.
[05:05] Priya: Can we use BYOK? Our key management policy requires we hold keys in our own KMS (Azure Key Vault).
[05:10] Samira: Yes, we support BYOK via KMS integrations: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For private deployments you can provide keys that never leave your environment, and we support HSM-backed keys for key wrapping.
[05:22] Maya: Tie that back to encryption at rest. If we bring our own keys, are models/parameters encrypted with our key, or just the data blobs?
[05:29] Samira: Customer data blobs (inputs and outputs) and the model artifact cache can be encrypted with customer-managed keys. The runtime's internal ephemeral caches are encrypted in transit; for fully on-prem or VPC deployments the model weights remain under customer control if you choose that option. I’ll share a diagram of the key flows.

[06:15] [Short cross-talk: Jordan confirming next docs to share]

[07:00] Ethan: About audit logs retention windows — legal wants at least 2 years of immutable audit trails with tamper evidence. Is that possible?
[07:08] Liam (CSM): In hosted mode our standard retention for audit logs is 13 months, but we have an enterprise tier that can extend to multi-year retention with WORM-style storage and S3 object locking. For Private, you can use your own logging stack and meet the two-year requirement.
[07:24] Maya: If we choose hosted with extended retention, who manages access controls to those logs? Can we restrict Redwood engineers from viewing content?
[07:33] Samira: With enterprise-hosted extended retention we can gate log access behind RBAC and show you the RBAC model; we can also provide a read-only bucket you manage and restrict Redwood's access, or present logs via an auditing API. We will include details in the security packet.

[08:05] Jordan: Let's talk RBAC and SSO. We support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and fine-grained roles. Samira, want to walk through roles quickly?
[08:14] Samira: Sure. We have built-in roles: org_admin, billing_admin, dev_ops, read_only, and a model_operator role for runtime-specific actions. Roles map to IAM policies and we support custom roles. SCIM provisioning can auto-populate user groups from your IdP.
[08:28] Priya: Can we restrict who can export prompts or who can run ad-hoc traces that would capture full request payloads?
[08:34] Samira: Yes — export and trace permissions are separate entitlements. We can lock traces behind higher roles and require MFA for any debug exports.

[09:00] Ethan: About data residency — our clinical data must remain in EU and can't cross borders. Does Redwood have regions and private deployments in EU?
[09:08] Jordan: Yes, we operate across NA, EU, and APAC regions. For strict residency we recommend Private VPC in the target region or Dedicated capacity reserved in the EU region. We can provide a map of regions and PS timeline for provisioning dedicated pools.
[09:23] Maya: If a eu-resident user triggers a model call, is the KV cache or any metadata routed to NA for performance?
[09:30] Samira: No, routing policies can be pinned to region. For EU deployments we can pin the control plane and runtime to EU to avoid cross-border movement.

[10:05] Jordan: A question from procurement — does Redwood sign standard DPAs and data residency annexes?
[10:12] Liam: We have a standard DPA and also addenda for data residency and no-training commitments. We can present the DPA and the no-training clause explicitly in the agreement.

[11:00] Maya: Quick follow-up — you mentioned ephemeral telemetry retention and X days. Can you confirm the default value and whether that can be shortened to zero?
[11:08] Samira: Default for hosted telemetry is 30 days for debug traces, but we can contractually reduce it or set it to zero for enterprise customers with Private deployments. We'll confirm exact SLA'd numbers in the packet.

[12:40] Ethan: In terms of proof — can you provide attestations that customer data is never used to update model weights? Sometimes vendors provide machine-readable lineage or audit trails showing training sources.
[12:52] Jordan: We have a documented policy and technical segregation in our infra — logs that are used for operational improvements are separated from any training pipelines and there is no link to our model training clusters. We'll share the architecture docs and the legal clause in the DPA.
[13:05] Priya: Are there any telemetry or metadata fields that are mandatory for safety or rate-limiting that would still include small snippets of prompts?
[13:14] Samira: We try to avoid capturing prompt text in telemetry; mandatory fields are token count and a truncated hash for dedupe. For safety signals we have an opt-in mechanism. We’ll provide a telemetry schema.

[15:00] [Jordan shares link in chat: https://redwood-inference.example/sec/SOC2-TypeII.pdf — note: link placeholder]

[16:22] Maya: Looking at the link — it references third-party pentest: is the scope of the pentest full-stack or just host perimeter?
[16:30] Liam: The pentest covers the platform control plane and network perimeter; for private deployments the customer is responsible for the host-level posture, but we provide a runbook and hardening checklist used by previous customers.

[18:00] Ethan: For our lawyers — is there any circumstance where Redwood would be compelled to disclose data to government requests? Jurisdictional escape hatches?
[18:10] Jordan: Any legal compulsion depends on where data resides. For EU-resident data we default to EU controls; for Private deployments the customer retains custody. We'll provide our process for lawful requests and our transparency reporting.

[20:05] Samira: Wanted to highlight one technical nuance: when you run the runtime in VPC with BYOK, we still have orchestration telemetry for health checks; customers can opt to route that telemetry to their logging endpoints rather than Redwood's systems so we don't see payloads.
[20:24] Priya: That's good. Can you show the network diagram and where KMS keywrap happens?
[20:31] Samira: Yes — I'll attach a diagram. Keywrap happens in the customer's KMS; Redwood only sees encrypted blobs and uses a key-wrapping key for the runtime bootstrap that is ephemeral.

[22:40] [Short pause; notes about scheduling deep-dive]

[24:10] Ethan: About retention of generated content — some of our workflows store model outputs in long-term storage. If outputs include PHI, we need control over retention TTLs. Can those be managed?
[24:22] Samira: Absolutely. Outputs written to customer buckets can be TTL-managed by the customer. For any outputs persisted in Redwood-managed caches we can configure TTLs or avoid persisting entirely in Private deployments.

[27:00] Jordan: We should also call out versioning — we let customers pin specific model revisions, and by default model updates do not happen automatically. That's important for regulatory traceability.
[27:10] Maya: Good — so if we pin to a model release, we can run our validation suite and then request rollout to newer version?
[27:16] Samira: Exactly. We support canary rollouts, A/B splits, and automatic fallback policies.

[30:05] Priya: On the BYOK HSM requirement — do you support FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs for key storage?
[30:12] Samira: We support HSM-backed keys via KMS and we can accommodate FIPS-validated HSMs depending on the cloud provider. For on-prem HSMs we have a provisioning guide.

[32:00] Ethan: A practical question — if we want zero-training and zero-telemetry, can we run a pilot to validate that no logs exit our VPC? We'd like Redwood to run an attestation and let us run a packet-capture.
[32:12] Samira: Yes — customers have done internal smoke tests. We can agree to a pilot scope: Redwood will run the runtime in your test VPC with BYOK, disable telemetry, and you can validate network flows. We'll provide a signed attestation after successful verification.

[35:20] Jordan: A couple of procurement notes — our standard timelines for Private deployments are 6-8 weeks for small pilots, 8-12 for full prod depending on infra. We'll put an initial SOW estimate in the packet.

[36:45] Maya: Our legal will also need a list of sub-processors and a clear clause about no-model-training.
[36:52] Liam: We'll include our sub-processor list and the no-training clause verbatim in the DPA.

[38:00] [Brief filler / small talk about holiday schedules]

[39:12] Ethan: On encryption in transit — do you support mTLS for all service-to-service calls?
[39:18] Samira: Yes, we use TLS 1.3 and support mTLS for private deployments. For hosted API keys we use per-org API keys and certificate-based mutual auth is an option for dedicated/private setups.

[41:00] Priya: If we require RBAC auditability, do you expose admin audit events in a machine-readable format (e.g., JSON event stream)?
[41:08] Samira: Yes — audit logs are available via API and can be streamed to your SIEM. Events include user, action, timestamp, outcome, and resource. We can increase verbosity on request.

[43:30] Maya: Two quick clarifications: 1) Is there any model telemetry stored that could be reconstructed into customer prompts? 2) Do you keep any permanent user-identifiers tied to prompt text?
[43:44] Samira: 1) No full prompt storage in default operational telemetry; hashed identifiers are used for deduping. 2) We avoid permanent tie-ins to user-identifiers; any mapping for debugging is ephemeral and access-controlled. We'll provide the telemetry schema and retention windows.

[46:00] Jordan: Okay I'd like to recap and make sure we have clear next steps — we've agreed to: share SOC 2 / ISO docs, DPA with explicit no-training clause, telemetry schema and retention numbers, BYOK runbook, and schedule a VPC deep-dive.
[46:15] Maya: Yes. Also please include the pentest scope and sub-processor list.
[46:20] Jordan: Noted.

[48:32] Ethan: One last ask — can Redwood include a short statement in the DPA that if there is ever a model update using external public corpuses, customer data will not be included? We want the language explicit beyond "not used for training".
[48:45] Liam: We can add a clause that explicitly states customer-specific data — prompts, attachments, logs — are excluded from any training datasets and that any aggregate telemetry used for product improvement will be anonymized and cannot be used to reconstruct prompts. We'll run the exact wording by legal.

[50:10] Priya: For scheduling the VPC deep-dive, I'm available next Tuesday or Thursday morning CET.
[50:18] Jordan: Let's tentatively slot Thursday 2026-12-16 09:00 CET — Samira and Priya as leads, Jordan to coordinate. We'll send a calendar invite.

[52:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, this helped a lot. We'll review the packet when you send it and get back to procurement.
[52:08] Jordan: Great — we'll send the docs by Friday 2026-12-11. Thanks all.
[52:15] [Meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: Some speaker overlaps, a few OCR-like misrecognitions in auto notes; attendees corrected acronyms (e.g., KV cache vs K/V) during call.
questions: Can Redwood provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO artifacts?
Does Redwood support BYOK and HSM-backed keywrap?
Can telemetry be disabled / set to zero retention for Private deployments?
Will Redwood sign a DPA with explicit no-training clause?
